description: Appointment to the Post of Director General of the Department of Government Factory
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-13 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The post of Director General of the Department of Government Factory has fallen vacant since 2026-07-09 following the retirement of                                               Mr. A. Wijesinghe, who served as the Director General of the said Post. The proposal made by the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply to appoint Eng. S.N.B.M. Padmasiri, Special Grade Officer of the Sri Lanka Engineering Service, who is presently serving as the Additional Director General of the Department of Government Factory, to the post of Director General of the Department of Government Factories, with immediate effect, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of a Centralized Zero-Waste Biomass Cinnamon Processing Centre as a Joint Project of the Industrial Technology Institute, University of Ruhuna and the Ministry of Science and Technology
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-13 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Cinnamon Industry in Sri Lanka, which is centred on small-scale growers in the Matara and Galle districts, continues to face a number of common challenges such as high processing costs, hygiene standards and minimal use of biomass waste. As a solution to these constraints, the Industrial Technology Institute in collaboration with the University of Ruhuna and the Ministry of Science and Technology have planned to establish a modern Centralized Zero waste Biomass Cinnamon Processing Centre at the premises of the Faculty of Agriculture of the University of Ruhuna, Mapalana. The project is expected to be implemented as a four-phase development project spanning a period of 27 months. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Science and Technology to establish the proposed Centralized Biomass Zero Waste Cinnamon Processing Centre at the premises of the Mapalana Faculty of Agriculture of the University of Ruhuna as a joint project between the Ministry of Science and Technology, the Industrial Technology Institute and the University of Ruhuna, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Capacity Enhancement Project of the Departure Passenger Terminal at the Bandaranaike International Airport, Katunayake
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-13 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-02-09 to implement the procurement process for the construction of a new building for thirty six (36) check-in counters and six (06) new Satellite boarding Gates from the passenger terminal under the Infrastructure Development Project for Departing Passenger Capacity Enhancement at the Bandaranaike International Airport, Katunayake. Bids have been invited to select a suitable contractor for the purpose by following the International Competitive Procurement Procedure and three (03) bids have been received for the same. The proposal made by the Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation to award the said contract to M/s Maga Engineering (Pvt) Ltd., the substantially responsive lowest bidder, based on the recommendation submitted by the Standing High Level Procurement Committee after evaluation of the said bids, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the Contract for the completion of the balance work of the Warakapola By Pass Road
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-13 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It is planned to complete the remaining construction works of the Warakapola Bypass road (Ch 0+000 to 2+320 km) using the funds allocated under the Widening and Improvement of National Highways Programme. Bids have been invited under the National Competitive Procurement Procedure to select a suitable contractor for the same, and six (06) bids have been received. Based on the recommendation submitted by the High-Level Procurement Committee following the evaluation of the said bids, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to award the said contract to M/s Maga Engineering (Pvt) Ltd., substantially responsive lowest bidder, for a sum of Rs.4.99 billion (excluding VAT), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Hosting the Fourth Meeting of the Ministers of Agriculture and the Meeting of the Senior Officials of the BIMSTEC in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-13 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) is a regional organization comprising seven South Asian and East Asian countries namely Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. The primary objective of the said organization is to promote economic cooperation among the countries adjacent to the Bay of Bengal. Taking into consideration that agriculture is a primary source of employment in the BIMSTEC member countries and recognizing the importance of agriculture and its related sectors for sustainable development and regional food security, agriculture has been included as one of the areas of BIMSTEC cooperation. Under this, the BIMSTEC Meeting of Agriculture Ministers and the Meeting of Senior Officials are held every two years, and it has been proposed to hold its fourth meeting in Sri Lanka. Accordingly, the proposal submitted by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to host the Fourth Meeting of the Ministers of Agriculture and Meeting of the Senior Officials of the BIMSTEC in Sri Lanka on 17th and 18th March 2027, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: National Livestock Policy
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-13 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been identified that the current National Livestock Policy, formulated in the year 2006, is required to be updated taking into account the challenges that have arisen in the field of food security and livestock development due to global and local social and economic transformations. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to implement the National Livestock Policy, formulated by obtaining local expert advice and knowledge and covering areas such as private sector-led development, market-oriented competitive production, sustainable and environmental responsible development, support for small-scale farmers and rural livelihoods, and science and technology based development, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Partnership for Energy Efficiency Building Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-13 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been planned to implement a Partnership for Energy Efficiency Building Programme under a Financial Grant provided as per the original Agreement regarding technical co-operation between the Federal Republic of Germany and the Republic of Sri Lanka. The programme is scheduled to be implemented by the GIZ (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit GmbH) of the Federal Republic of Germany and monitored by the Ministry of Energy and the Sustainable Energy Authority. The main objective of the programme is to support Sri Lanka in obtaining policies, institutional frameworks and technical assistance for the maintenance of energy-efficient and climate-resilient buildings. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Energy to sign an Agreement among the Ministry of Energy, the Department of External Resources and the Country Representative of GIZ to implement the said programme under a total Financial Grant of EUR 924,063 (approximately 314 million Sri Lankan Rupees), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Rooftop Solar Aggregation and Virtual Net Metering Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-13 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The "the Rooftop Solar Aggregation and Virtual Net Metering Project" has been identified as a priority project with the aim of improving small and medium-scale renewable energy projects by offering a streamlined solution for independent power producers to use and distribute the solar energy effectively. Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-11-03 to conduct negotiations with the Asian Development Bank and other relevant agencies regarding the financing of the said project. As per the said decision, negotiations with the Asian Development Bank, the European Union and the Japan Fund for the Joint Crediting Mechanism for obtaining relevant Loans and Grants have been concluded as of now. The proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to enter into Loan and Grant Agreements with the Asian Development Bank to obtain a loan of US$ 35 million from the Concessional Ordinary Capital Resources of the ADB, a Grant of EUR 15.4 million from the European Union and a Grant of US$ 5.5 million from the Japan Fund for the Joint Crediting Mechanism, based on the agreement reached during the said discussions and subject to the terms and conditions of the Asian Development Bank loan, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: National Policy of Sri Lanka on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering the Financing of Terrorism and Counter Proliferation Financing for 2026-2030
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-13 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Financial crimes such as Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Proliferation Financing of weapons of mass destruction pose serious threats to the Sri Lanka’s economy and the global financial system. With rapid technological advancements, financial transactions have become more sophisticated, and it has become a challenging task to identify and disrupt the methods used by criminals to hide the proceeds of crime. Therefore, the Financial Intelligence Unit of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka has conducted the third National Risk Assessment of Sri Lanka on Financial Crimes for the period 2024/25 in accordance with the standards set by the Financial Action Task Force, an intergovernmental policy-making body dealing with financial crimes. In order to manage the risks identified in the said National Risk Assessment, the "National Policy of Sri Lanka on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering the Financing of Terrorism and Counter Proliferation Financing for 2026-2030" has been prepared. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to implement the said National Policy during the period 2026-2030, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Committee Stage amendments to the Financial Transactions Reporting (Amendment) Bill and the Prevention of Money Laundering (Amendment) Bill
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-06 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Cabinet approval has been granted on 2026-02-09 to publish the Financial Transactions Reporting (Amendment) Bill and the Prevention of Money Laundering (Amendment) Bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter submit the same to Parliament. The Legal Draftsman has drafted amendments proposed to be introduced at the Committee Stage of the said Bills in Parliament, incorporating the decisions of the Supreme Court pertaining to the cases filled challenging the said Amendment Bills and several essential amendments identified. The clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the said new amendments. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to present the said amendments at the Committee Stage of the said Bills in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment to the Post of Commissioner of Probation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-06 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Ms. U.L. Mathisha Jinanjalie Jayathilake, Grade I Officer of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service, presently serving as the Director (Development) of the Ministry of Justice and National Integration, has been identified as suitable for the Post of Commissioner of Probation which is vacant at present. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Women and Child Affairs to appoint                 Ms. U.L. Mathisha Jinanjalie Jayathilake, to the Post of Commissioner of the Department of Probation and Child Care Services with immediate effect, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of Regulations issued under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, No. 1 of 1969, to Parliament for approval
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-06 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2026-03-30, granted approval for making it mandatory to obtain Export Control License for items such as scrap metal products, various metal replicas and metal scrap in order to prevent illegal export of such goods with a view to protecting local industrialists. The Imports and Exports (Control) Regulations, No.05 of 2026 have been published in the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.2493/03 dated 2026-06-15, to give effect to that decision.Further, the Imports and Exports (Control) Regulations, No.06 of 2026 have been published in the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.2493/39 dated 2026-06-18 under the provisions of the Import and Export (Control) Act, No.1 of 1969, amending the Special Import License and Payment Regulations, No.1 of 2011, dated 2012-01-02, enabling to introduce new provisions to ensure that goods imported under the Advance Payment, which is an approved payment system for international trade, are brought into Sri Lanka within the prescribed period of 180, 365 or 730 days from the date of remittance of payment, as specified in the relevant regulations. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to submit the Regulations published in the said Gazette Notifications to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Expanding the scope of the Kandy City Wastewater Management Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-06 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Kandy City Wastewater Management Project has been implemented under 04 packages since 2010 under a Loan Agreement signed with the Japan International Cooperation Agency. Approval was granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-01-12 to extend the project period of the said project from 2025-01-01 to 2027-08-31. Based on the results of a feasibility study conducted at the request of the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Peradeniya to include the University of Peradeniya premises in the scope of the said project, it has been identified that the said University can also be included in the scope of the project. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply to include the University of Peradeniya under the scope of the Kandy City Wastewater Management Project, to secure Rs.800 million from the loan of the Japan International Cooperation Agency and the remaining Rs.1,200 million from local funds, out of the estimated cost of Rs.2,000 million, and to further extend the project period up to 2027-12-31, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Payment of compensation for patients who lost vision following the administration of Prednisolone Acetate medication after eye surgeries
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-06 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - There have been reports of several patients who underwent eye surgeries at the Nuwara Eliya District General Hospital losing or further deteriorating their eyesight due to the use of Prednisolone Acetate Ophthalmic Suspension during the period between 2023-03-03 and 2023-05-16. Based on the results of an investigation into that matter, compensation has been provided to 17 patients who lost their eyesight after undergoing eye surgeries at the Nuwara Eliya District General Hospital by now. In addition, the Expert Technical Committee appointed to examine and report on patients who suffered eye problems due to the use of the Prednisolone Acetate Ophthalmic Suspension during eye surgeries at hospitals other than the Nuwara Eliya District General Hospital during the relevant period, has recommended the payment of compensation for 04 more patients as well, who became blind. Accordingly, taking into account the matters furnished by the Minister of Health and Mass Media, it was decided to grant the concurrence of the Cabinet to provide compensation for the four patients at the rate of one million Rupees per patient.

description: Further expansion of the Vessel Monitoring System for Multi-Day Fishing Vessels and IDAY Fishing Vessels in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-06 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A major challenge faced by Sri Lanka, as well as many fishing nations around the world, is suppression of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and other unlawful activities carried out using fishing vessels including drug trafficking, human trafficking, and the transport of illegal cargo. Various measures have been taken at the local, regional and international levels to combat this situation. At the regional level, Sri Lanka is a member of the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission, and according to the rules of the Commission, every fishing vessel engaged in international waters are required to be continuously monitored by the Vessel Monitoring System (VMS). Currently, out of the 5,200 registered multi-day fishing vessels operating in Sri Lanka, 4,200 multi-day fishing vessels have been equipped with monitoring systems, which were received as a Grant from the Australian Government. Since it is mandatory to install VMS for every newly registered multi-day fishing vessel after 2021-01-01, vessel owners purchase and install VMS equipment in vessels registered from that date. There are approximately 1,500 multi-day fishing vessels and IDAY fishing vessels without VMS that were registered as multi-day fishing vessels before 2021-01-01 and are operating in domestic waters and sometimes in international waters. Of these, 400 vessels with a length of more than 34 feet can be used for fishing or other activities in international waters at any time. In addition, remaining 1,100 vessels are those that do not have sufficient technical suitability to remain at sea for extended periods, given their engine capacity and fuel capacity. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Fisheries, Aquatic and Ocean Resources to make it mandatory for those 1,500 vessels to install appropriate monitoring systems and for the Government to bear the cost thereof, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: ‘Sri Lanka Expo 2027’ International Exhibition
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-06 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2026-04-27, granted approval to hold the ‘Sri Lanka Expo 2027’ International Exhibition from 2027-01-14 to 2027-01-17. Quotations have been invited to select an entity for Event Management of the said Exhibition and 03 bids have been received for the same. The proposal made by the Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development to award the said procurement to Lanka Exhibition and Conference Services (Pvt) Limited (LECS) JV with Aitken Spence Travels (Pvt) Ltd. (ASTL), as the substantially responsive bidder, at a sum of Rs.178.71 million (inclusive of VAT), based on the recommendation submitted by the Cabinet Appointed Consultant Procurement Committee after evaluating the said bids, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding Consultancy Service Contract for carrying out a structural analysis of the existing road-cum-aqueduct structure located at 3+685km of the Right Bank Canal under the Rajanganaya Irrigation Scheme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-06 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The aqueduct structure across the Angamuwa spill canal at 3+685km of the Right Bank Canal of the Rajanganaya Irrigation Scheme has been constructed in the year 1966 integrating the road connecting the Rajanganaya Reservoir to the Rajanganaya Junction on the Puttalam-Anuradhapura road. As about 60 years have lapsed since the construction of the said structure and the number of vehicles travelling from the Rajanganaya Reservoir to the Rajanganaya Junction has increased significantly, the existing integrated road- cum-aqueduct structure has severely deteriorated. Under the circumstances, the Road Development Authority has agreed to construct a separate new bridge across the Angamuwa spill canal to meet the current traffic requirements, and a comprehensive structural analysis needs to be carried out expeditiously to determine whether the aqueduct structure can be rehabilitated or if not, whether the structure should be reconstructed. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Lands and Irrigation to award the consultancy service contract for carrying out the analysis to the Central Engineering Consultancy Bureau, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the World Habitat Day Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-06 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The United Nations has declared the first Monday of October every year as World Habitat Day. World Habitat Day is celebrated with the aim of drawing the attention of all stakeholders to the problems, alternative solutions and emerging trends related to housing and human settlement development and to raise awareness among all stakeholders through the establishment of a national-level dialogue, thereby ensuring the reach of benefits of such efforts to all people without delay. World Habitat Day 2026 falls on 05 October, and its theme has been declared as 'Adequate Housing for all'. The Ministry in charge of the subject of Housing, as the Sri Lankan representative institution of the United Nations Human Settlements Programme, which implements World Habitat Day worldwide, has planned to organize the World Habitat Day celebration programme this year as well, with the participation of relevant Ministries and all Institutions. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply to implement the World Habitat Day Programme 2026 in collaboration with the relevant Ministries and Institutions, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Commencement of a Bus Sector Clustering Pilot Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-07-06 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Bus transport is the main mode of transport used to meet the daily passenger transportation requirements of the country, and the said service is operated by the Sri Lanka Transport Board and a large number of independent private bus operators. As a result of the said operational mode being operated in providing passenger transport service, many problems have arisen such as excessive competition, poor adherence to scheduled timetables, excessive concentration of buses on certain routes, unsafe driving practices, inconvenience faced by passengers, traffic congestion, service imbalances and inefficient use of resources. As a successful solution to such problems, 'Bus Sector Clustering' has been introduced in many countries of the world and bus services operating in the same transport corridor or geographical area are operated under an integrated management. It has been identified that the introduction of bus sector clustering, a method of managing bus services operating on interconnected routes not as separate and independent operating units but as an integrated and coordinated service cluster, to Sri Lanka has the potential to provide an effective passenger transport service and minimize many of the operational and social problems currently existing in the bus sector. Accordingly, taking into account the matters submitted by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development, the Cabinet granted its concurrence for the implementation of a bus sector clustering pilot programme in bus corridors covering bus routes 170, 177 and 190 with the participation of relevant stakeholders in the first instance and to further expand the said programme based on its results.

description: Obtaining financial assistance of the Government of India for the implementation effort of rehabilitation and reconstruction programmes in Sri Lanka in the aftermath of the Cyclone 'Ditwah'
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The reconstruction needs of about US$ 3.5 billion have been identified for the physical damage of US$ 2.1 billion and economic damage of US$ 1.4 billion as a result of the impact caused to Sri Lanka in November 2025 by Cyclone 'Ditwah'. During the disaster period, the Government of India provided the necessary assistance for disaster relief and emergency response activities under 'Operation Sagar Bandhu'. At the discussion held during the visit of the Hon. Minister of Foreign Affairs of India to Sri Lanka on 2025-12-22, it was agreed to provide a disaster relief package to Sri Lanka under 'Operation Sagar Bandhu'. Under this, the Government of India has proposed a relief package of US$ 450 million in the form of a line of credit of US$ 350 million and a grant of US$ 100 million. It has further been agreed that the credit facility of US$ 350 million will be provided in the form of a long‑term line of credit of US$ 250 million and a short-term line of credit of US$ 100 million, and a grant of US$ 100 million will be provided so as to cover the areas of infrastructure, connectivity, health, education, housing, water supply and disaster management. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to enter into relevant agreements between the two parties to obtain the proposed credit facility, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Purchase of Paddy in the Yala Season 2026
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to secure provisions of Rs.6,000 million to implement the programme for the purchase of Paddy for the Yala Season 2026, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Automating the operations of the Bank Supervision Department of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Bank Supervision Department of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka carries out regulation and supervision activities of licensed banks with the aim of ensuring the stability and soundness of the banking system. In order to accomplish those functions, extensive interactions are maintained with licensed banks and other stakeholders, and a large number of regulatory and supervisory documents are prepared, reviewed, stored and retrieved. The majority of these functions are performed through physical records management, and the implementation of a technology-driven supervisory solution to improve the efficiency of these functions has been identified as a priority for the Bank Supervision Department. Accordingly, based on a needs assessment conducted with the technical assistance of the Asian Development Bank, the proposal made by the                        Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to implement the procurement process for the provision of a technology-driven supervisory solution for the Bank Supervision Department of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment to the Post of Director General of Meteorology
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The post of Director General of the Department of Meteorology is currently vacant. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as Minister of Defence to appoint Mr. A.L.K. Wijemannage, the most senior Officer in the Special Grade of the Sri Lanka Scientific Service serving in the Department, who is currently serving as the Additional Director General of the Department, to the post of Director General of the Department of Meteorology with immediate effect, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs Bill
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-09-22 to prepare a Bill to consolidate the Rabies Ordinance (Chapter 476) and the Dog Registration Ordinance (Chapter 477) with the objective of controlling the dog population, regularizing and making mandatory the administration of rabies vaccination for dogs, strengthening legal provisions relating to the registration of dogs, clarifying the powers and responsibilities of the institutions responsible for those functions, and establishing a mechanism for the implementation of those responsibilities. Accordingly, the clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman. The proposal made by the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government to publish the said Bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter submit the same to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Completion of the Construction of the Four-Storied Building of the National Hospital, Kandy
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - During the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021, a project for the construction of a pre‑fabricated four-storied building with 50 negative pressure isolation rooms for the Kandy National Hospital was initiated at an estimated cost of US$ 1.2 million (approximately Rs.236 million). The project was financed through a grant from the SAARC Development Fund. During the implementation of the project, the original scope of the project was revised to reduce the number of isolation rooms from 50 to 23, and to construct a 25-bed male ward and a 20-bed female ward, thereby increasing the total bed capacity from 50 to 68. Construction work worth Rs.282.24 million has been completed so far. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to revise the total cost estimate of the project to Rs.1,094.22 million and to extend the project period to 2027-12-31, to enable the completion of the project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: The Project for the Development of the Jaffna Town Hall Building
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2019-09-10 to award the contract for the construction of the Jaffna Town Hall Building to M/s Central Engineering Services (Pvt.) Ltd. The said construction work commenced on 2019-10-10 and has achieved about 70% physical progress as of 2022. However, owing to the economic crisis faced by the country in 2022, the said project could not be completed within the initial contract period due to insufficient funds. Based on the recommendations of the Public Investment Monitoring and Evaluation Committee, it has been planned to complete the construction of the said building up to Phase 2, including the air conditioning system. Following the said constructions, the Jaffna Municipal Council has agreed to take over the building to carry out the functions of the Jaffna Municipal Council. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to complete the works up to Phase 2 of the Jaffna Municipal Council Building construction project, by M/s Central Engineering Services (Pvt.) Ltd, the contractor of the said project, at a revised cost estimate of Rs.1,958.85 million (excluding taxes), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement for the construction of section 1 (Kurunegala to Galewela) of the road section of phase 4 (Kurunegala to Dambulla) of the Central Expressway Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-03-03 for the construction of the road section of Phase 4 of the Central Expressway Project, from Kurunegala to Dambulla. The Cabinet Appointed Special Committee on Economic Management having discussed the sources of funding, decided to implement the Phase 4 of road section of the Central Expressway Project in two Phases, and to implement the Phase 1 of road section of 38.5 km from Kurunegala to Galewela (Ch. 78+000 km to Ch. 116+500 km) using the funds of the Government of Sri Lanka. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to implement the procurement process to enable the implementation of Phase 1 (Kurunegala to Galewela) of the road section of Phase 4 of the Central Expressway Project through local contractors, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement of Urea Fertilizer to State Fertilizer Company Limited for the Maha Season 2026/27
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It is estimated that 800,000 hectares of paddy land will be cultivated with paddy and other crops in the Maha Season 2026/27. Approximately 169,635 MT of Urea is required for such cultivations as per the chemical fertilizer recommendations of the Department of Agriculture. In addition, urea fertilizer should be supplied for plantation crops, vegetables, fruit crops and other crops both as straight fertilizer and for preparation of mixed fertilizers. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Lands and Irrigation to purchase 10,000 MT of Urea (Prilled) and 10,000 MT of Urea (Granular) to State Fertilizer Company Limited for the Maha Season 2026/27 by following the international competitive bidding procedure to meet the said Urea Fertilizer requirement, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Cyclone ‘Ditwah’ Recovery Projects
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In accordance with the provisions of the Public Financial Management Act, No.44 of 2024, public investment projects specifically developed in response to natural disasters or emergencies declared by the Government can be considered outside the Public Investment Programme and such projects shall be approved by the Cabinet. The proposals submitted to the Department of National Planning for the restoration of the damages caused to the people, their livelihoods, public infrastructure and essential services caused by Cyclone 'Ditwah' have been reviewed and recommendations have been made by the said Department, paying attention to the policy of 'Building Back Better'. The recommendations have been considered by the Public Investment Committee and appropriate modes of financing have been identified for each project. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to implement 1,028 of Cyclone ‘Ditwah’ recovery projects from the year 2026 onwards at an estimated cost of Rs.515,460.26 million, by securing provisions through the Annual Budget, and in addition, to implement 38 recovery projects by Provincial Councils at an estimated cost of Rs.102,219.05 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement for the installation of a new Core Banking System for the Bank of Ceylon
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The current Core Banking System of the Bank of Ceylon, International Comprehensive Banking System, is being used for 22 years for both retail and corporate businesses, including its overseas branches. It has been observed that many of the features and functionalities of the said system, as well as the technology underlying it, are inadequate to meet the present day banking demands. Therefore, the Board of Directors of the Bank of Ceylon has approved the recommendations made to install a new Core Banking System instead of further upgrading the said banking system. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to implement the procurement for the selection of a suitable service provider to establish a new Core Banking System in the Bank of Ceylon for a period of 05 years at an estimated cost of US$ 10 million using the funds of the said Bank, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Programme for providing a pair of footwear each for the selected school students, lay and clergy students of Pirivena and Seela Mathas for the year 2027
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The programme for providing a pair of footwear to the selected school students, lay/ clergy students of Pirivenas and Seela Mathas for the year 2026 was implemented under two methodologies, covering a total of 836,571 school and Pirivena students. The programme for providing a pair of footwear for the year 2027 is planned to be completed by the end of the third school term of 2026. Accordingly, taking into account the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, the Cabinet granted its approval for the implementation of the said programme by providing a coupon worth Rs.3,000/- each to the selected school students, lay and clergy students of Pirivenas and Seela Mathas for the purchase of footwear brought to the school by local footwear manufacturers in the Western, Southern, Sabaragamuwa, Eastern and North Western provinces, and for the purchase of footwear from the market in the Central, Northern, North Central and Uva provinces, based on the progress of the methodology implemented in the year 2026.

description: Taking over the District General Hospital - Horana under the Line Ministry of Health and Mass Media
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Horana Hospital, which functioned as a base hospital, was upgraded to the level of a District General Hospital on 2022-06-03 and is currently administered under the Western Provincial Council. At present, the hospital has a total bed capacity of 544 and an approved cadre of 739. The hospital, which is centrally located covering the Horana area and its surrounding areas of Kalutara, Colombo and Ratnapura Districts, provides healthcare services to a population of approximately one million. In view of the need to increase the relevant facilities and human resources to provide tertiary care services as a District General Hospital, it has been identified as appropriate to take over the said hospital under the Ministry of Health and Mass Media. The concurrence of the Hon. Governor of the Western Province has been received for the same. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to take over the District General Hospital - Horana, including all physical and financial assets, under the Ministry of Health and Mass Media, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Revising the bus fare
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-30 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - According to the bus fare policy currently in force, the National Transport Commission is required to announce the revision of bus fares on 01st July every year. Accordingly, the National Transport Commission has appointed a Committee to submit recommendations for updating and revising the existing bus fare formula (cost index) and fare structure, paying attention to the frequent fluctuations in fuel prices due to the war situation prevailing in the Middle East region from February 2026, and the associated operating costs, the types of buses currently in service, the impact of fluctuations in the value of the US dollar on the cost of bus spare parts, buses operating on expressways and the low-floor buses recently introduced operating under Lanka Metro Transit (Private) Limited, and taking into account the provision of continuous transport services to the public and the safety of the bus industry. The proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to revise bus fares by the National Transport Commission, taking also into account the fuel price revision made to be effective from 2026-06-30, as per the recommendations submitted by the said Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment of a Special Cabinet Sub-Committee and an Official’s Committee to address the impact of the El Niño Climate Condition
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- As Sri Lanka is a country highly sensitive to climate change, the risk of occurring changes in rainfall patterns in the country, high temperature and disaster situations such as droughts and floods remain at a very high level due the global climate phenomenon known as El Niño. Consequently, there is a potential for adverse impacts on numerous economic and social sectors. The Government has identified the need to take urgent measures to address the intensity and impact of El Niño conditions, which are confirmed by scientific predictions to occur from the end of this year onwards with the impact of climate change. Therefore, it has been decided to implement a national-level action plan by strengthening coordination among Government institutions, Local Authorities, Non-governmental organizations, Private Sector and community organizations to minimize the possible impacts. Accordingly, the proposal made by the                        Hon. President to take the following steps, was approved by the Cabinet:

(i)	to appoint a Cabinet Sub Committee comprising of the following Ministers to take immediate action for formulating short term, medium term and annual action plans for the management of the water, electricity and food crisis arising due to the El Niño condition, to ensure integrated operations among all Government entities and minimize the disaster risk by making public awareness:


*	Hon. (Dr.) Dammika Patabendi,
	Minister of Environment - (Chairman).

*	Hon. K.D. Lal Kantha,
	Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation

*	Hon. Samantha Viddyarathna,
	Minister of Plantation and Community Infrastructure.

*	Hon. Anura Karunathilaka,
	Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation; and
	Minister of Energy.

*	Hon. Wasantha Samarasinghe,
	Minister of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Cooperative Development.

*	Hon. (Dr.) Susil Ranasinghe,
	Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply.

 (ii)	to appoint an Officials' Committee with the following composition to assist the above Cabinet Sub Committee:

*	Chief of Staff to the President - (Chairman).

*	Secretary, Ministry of Environment.

*	Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation.

description: Submission of the Annual Report of the Public Debt Management Office for the year 2025 to Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: As per section 25 of the Public Debt Management Act, No.33 of 2024, the Public Debt Management Office shall prepare an Annual Report on Government borrowings of the Government and other debt management operations, outstanding public debt, guarantees and on-lending activities and other financing arrangements entered into during the previous financial year. Further, as mentioned in the said Act, the Minister in charge of the subject of Finance shall review the draft of the Annual Report and submit it to the Cabinet for approval, and thereafter the approved Annual Report shall be submitted to Parliament within 180 days of the end of the preceding financial year. The said Report approved by Parliament shall also be published on the official websites of the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development and the Public Debt Management Office. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, for the Annual Report prepared by the Public Debt Management Office for the year ended as at 2025 12 31 and for the submission of the said Annual Report to Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Fiscal Strategy Statement – 2027
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In accordance with the provisions of the Public Financial Management Act, No.44 of 2024, medium-term strategies should be prepared and implemented with the objective of enhancing fiscal transparency and accountability. As per section 11 of the said Act, the Minister in charge of the subject of Finance should prepare and submit the Fiscal Strategy Statement along with the Medium-Term Fiscal Framework annually. The Fiscal Strategy Statement provides the strategic basis for the preparation of the national budget which includes the fiscal objectives, targets and policies of the Government. As per the provisions of the Public Financial Management Act, the Fiscal Strategy Statement should specifically indicate the main sources of fiscal risks towards the achievement of fiscal objectives together with an estimate of the fiscal impact of such fiscal risks. The Fiscal Strategy Statement shall be submitted for approval by the Cabinet and shall thereafter be tabled in Parliament by the Minister of Finance on or before 30th June of the relevant year. The Annual Budget shall be prepared on the basis of the Fiscal Strategy Statement. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development for the Fiscal Strategy Statement for the year 2027 and for tabling the same in Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the National Commission for Research and Development
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Research and development activities are considered as an essential factor in accelerating a country's knowledge-based economic growth, promoting innovation, enhancing competitiveness, and achieving sustainable development goals which contribute the production of value-added goods and services, strengthening the human and social development and introducing innovative solutions to national problems, and managing sustainable environment. Due to the centralization of research and development activities in this country in only a few limited areas, weak coordination between entities, and insufficient policy and financial support, it has not been possible to achieve the anticipated outcomes from the resources deployed for the same. Therefore, the need to establish a National Commission, similar to those established in developed countries, and an office equipped with capability and competency to execute its relevant functions has been identified, so as to establish an efficient and integrated mechanism that can link the entire process of research and development. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President to establish the National Commission for Research and Development in order to empower the research and development process that is carried out separately in various Ministries and Institutions, within a single framework and to effectively use the research outcomes, and to appoint a Committee to prepare a Preliminary Draft/Concept Paper to introduce legal provisions for the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Granting no-pay leave to officers entitled to political rights who contested at the Local Government Elections and elected as Deputy Mayors/Vice Chairmen of such institutions
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In accordance with the provisions of Public Administration Circular 12/2021 dated 2021 06 25, officers entitled to political rights who contested at the Local Government Elections and elected as Deputy Mayors/Vice Chairmen of such institutions are able to obtain 06 days leave with pay per month. However, if the said leave period is not adequate to attend the meetings of the relevant Local Government Authority and engage in related activities, it has been recommended in a discussion held under the chairmanship of the Director General of Establishments and with the participation of representatives of the relevant institutions that it would be appropriate to provide such officers with the opportunity to take no-pay leave. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government to issue Circular instructions amending the provisions of the Establishments Code, enabling the officers entitled to political rights who contested at the Local Government Elections and elected as Deputy Mayors/Vice Chairmen of such institutions to obtain no-pay leave, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Publishing the Animal Welfare Bill in the Government Gazette
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - An Expert Committee has been appointed by the Secretary to the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation, as per the Cabinet decision dated 2025.12.29, to examine the provisions of the Bill prepared pertaining to animal welfare and submit appropriate recommendations. The Legal Draftsman has been instructed at the Cabinet meeting held on 18.05.2026 to prepare the final Bill on Animal Welfare based on the recommendations submitted by the said Committee. Accordingly, the Legal Draftsman has prepared the Animal Welfare Bill, and the clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the same. The proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to publish the Bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter submit the same to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Removal of legal provisions on marking voters using indelible ink at Elections
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Under the legal provisions for Elections in the country, it is mandatory for voters who come to mark their votes at Elections/Polls to verify their identity through a valid identity card, and it is also mandatory for all such voters to mark them with an appropriate mark using indelible ink, since 2004. Both of these requirements are intended to prevent the casting of more than one vote by the same voter at a single election. It has been observed that following two different methods at the same time to achieve the same objective hinders the efficiency of the duties performed at polling stations and also incurs additional costs to the Government. Therefore, it has been found appropriate to remove the legal provisions regarding the use of indelible ink and marking the voter with the appropriate mark from all Election Acts. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President to take necessary steps to remove the following legal provisions, was approved by the Cabinet:

*	Section 36 of the Presidential Elections Act, No.15 of 1981

*	Section 38 of the Parliamentary Elections Act, No.1 of 1981

*	Section 36 of the Provincial Councils Elections Act, No.2 of 1988

*	Section 53A of the Local Authorities Elections Ordinance                (Chapter 262)

*	Section 21 of the Referendum Act, No. 7 of 1981.

description: Awarding of the contract for Passenger and Ground Handling Services of Sri Lankan Airlines at the Delhi Airport
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Bids have been invited following the Limited International Competitive Bidding Procedure to select a Ground Handling Service Provider for securing Passenger and Ramp Handling Services of Sri Lankan Airlines at the Delhi Airport. 02 bids have been received for the same. The proposal made by the Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation to award the said service providing contract to Bird Flight Services (India) Private Limited, the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, based on the recommendation submitted by the Standing High Level Procurement Committee after evaluation of the said bids, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Installation of the Aeronautical Message Handling System for Airport and Aviation Services (Sri Lanka) (Private) Limited
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Aeronautical Message Handling System serves are a vital platform for operational and safety-critical Aeronautical information between the stake holders of aviation sector within Sri Lanka, as well as internationally. Since the operational period of the existing Aeronautical Message Handling System of Airport and Aviation Services (Sri Lanka) (Private) Limited, the National Air Navigation Service Provider of Sri Lanka is nearing the termination, the need to provide, install and operate a modern system to replace the existing system has been identified. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation to initiate the relevant procurement process for the replacement of the Aeronautical Message Handling System at Ratmalana, at an estimated cost of Rs.1,000 million under the capital budget of Airport and Aviation Services (Sri Lanka) (Private) Limited, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Programme for the Electrification of Railway Lines
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- At present, the majority of railway operations in Sri Lanka are diesel-powered, and many railway lines, signalling systems and related infrastructure require upgrading to improve operational efficiency and service reliability. Therefore, with the aim of establishing a modern and sustainable railway transport system, the Government of Sri Lanka has initiated several railway development programmes focusing on the construction of new railway lines, double tracking, upgrading of signalling systems and electrification of railway lines. Accordingly, railway lines with high density corridors have been identified for electrification with the aim of improving transport capacity, reducing travel time and supporting environmentally sustainable public transportation. These development activities are expected to be implemented with the assistance of international development agencies, as part of the country’s long-term transport modernization strategy. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to take necessary action to construct the following railway lines with electrification, was approved by the Cabinet:

* 	Main Line - Railway line from Maradana to Ragama including the development of railway station buildings at Gampaha, Veyangoda, Mirigama and Polgahawela.

* 	Kelani Valley Line - Railway line from Maradana to Makumbura.

*	 Coastal Line - Railway line from Maradana to Panadura.

description: Japanese Grant Aid for Human Resources Development Scholarship Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Government of Japan has been supporting the professional development of young executive level public officials since 2010 under the Japanese Grant Aid for Human Resources Development Scholarship Programme. This programme has made a significant contribution to strengthening the capacity of the Government Service of Sri Lanka by providing opportunities for public officials to acquire advanced academic qualifications, professional expertise and international exposure in the fields relevant to national development priorities. The programme is financed under the Official Development Assistance Framework of the Government of Japan and is implemented by the Japan International Cooperation Agency. About 15 public officials are awarded scholarships under this programme annually, and so far opportunities for 255 Master’s Degree Programmes and 16 Doctoral Degree Programmes have been availed. The proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to obtain the grant of 282 million Japanese Yen (approximately 575 million rupees) agreed to be provided for the year 2026 under the said programme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Installation of a Computer Network for the Department of Examinations, Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Department of Examinations, Sri Lanka conducts over 300 examinations annually, including national level examinations, and a computerized management information system is used to manage all the data and critical tasks associated with the operations of those examinations. Since the main operational functions of the department exist as computer networks that are unique to each division, many critical stages of the examination process have to be handled using human resources only, and data and documents are transferred between branches through physical channels. As a result, it has been observed that there is a decrease in efficiency, delays, wastage of physical and human resources, etc. Therefore, it has been identified that it is essential to upgrade the computer network infrastructure of the Department of Examinations in line with the current digitalization process of public sector services. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister, in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, to design, install and operate a wide computer network covering all branches of the Department of Examinations Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Declaration of the National Legal Aid Day in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Legal Aid Commission of Sri Lanka was established under the Legal Aid Act No.27 of 1978 with the objective of facilitating access to justice for all citizens, including vulnerable groups and marginalized persons. The Commission makes a significant contribution to the protection of fundamental rights, strengthening the rule of law and promoting access to justice through the provision of legal aid services and promotion of legal awareness. The appropriateness of declaring a National Legal Aid Day has been identified with the objective of enhancing public awareness of legal rights and remedies, facilitating a national dialogue on law enforcement and enhancing public understanding of the importance of legal aid services. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice and National Integration to declare 06th July, the date of the enactment of the Legal Aid Act, No.27 of 1978, as the 'National Legal Aid Day in Sri Lanka' was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Island-Wide implementation of the ‘National Social and Behaviour Change Communication Programme for Child Health Promotion’ under the Clean Sri Lanka Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- It has been observed that poor physical and oral hygiene, excessive sugar and salt consumption, consumption of sweetened beverages and bakery products, lack of adequate physical exercise and sleep, addiction to digital screens, and insensitivity to the environment are prevalent among children under the age of 05 in Sri Lanka. Based on the available scientific evidence on the aforesaid issues and the National Multisectoral Strategic Action Plan on Early Childhood Care and Development 2025-2029 published by the Ministry of Women and Child Affairs, the Health Promotion Bureau, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders in early childhood health promotion, has developed a programme called ‘National Social and Behaviour Change Communication Programme for Child Health Promotion’ and implemented the same during the year 2025 with the financial support of UNICEF as follows:

* 	Selecting the preschool community as a practical and appropriate setting for the implementation of the said programme.

* 	Training 277 officers selected from the sectors of health, early childhood development and early childhood education as the master trainers of the programme.

* 	Training of teachers from 900 selected health promotion preschools covering all districts of Sri Lanka by those master trainers and providing them each with the necessary communication tool package to carry out the relevant activities in those preschools.

* 	Verifying the use of the relevant communication tool package by the Health Promotion Bureau and the feasibility of further use of that package, through a follow-up programme.
Taking into account the progress achieved by the implementation of the said programme in the year 2025, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to implement the ‘National Social and Behaviour Change Communication Programme for Child Health Promotion’ island wide under the STEP UP Early Childhood Development Programme initiated by the Clean Sri Lanka Programme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Admission of Children to Grade One of Schools
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Circular instructions are issued for each year regarding the admission of children to Grade One in government schools, and its objective is to make provisions so as to ensure equitable access to education with transparency and minimal irregularities. The new circular has been prepared, taking into account the views and suggestions of the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption, the Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka, principals and education authorities, and also focusing on new education reforms. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister, in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, to issue a new circular containing the relevant provisions and instructions for the admission of children to Grade One in government schools from the year 2027 onwards, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment of a Special Committee to protect Lands in the Eastern Province
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Several social, economic and administrative crises have emerged in the Eastern Province due to the misuse of political power and political favouritism as well as forcible encroachments of lands, unauthorized land reclamation and illegal coastal constructions. As a result, the natural ecosystem of the region has been severely endangered, and these haphazard and illegal human activities have also become the main cause for the rapid, severe coastal erosion affecting the entire coastline. Similarly, although 16 years have passed since the end of the civil war, failure to implement a formal procedure for the permanent resettlement of displaced people and deviations from the general criteria in establishing administrative structures have directly affected the development activities in the province as well as the national security. The Cabinet approved the implementation of the following proposals submitted by the Hon. President to seek prompt and permanent solutions to aforesaid issues, initiate legal action and strengthen institutional coordination:

* 	Appointment of a Committee titled ‘Protect Lands in the Eastern Province’ under the Chairmanship of Mr. Senaka Palliyaguruge, former Land Commissioner of the Southern Province and current Commissioner of Local Government of the Southern Province and comprising representatives of relevant institutions.

* 	Establishment of a Special Unit headed by a Deputy Inspector General of Police immediately and vesting full authority to the security forces to stop all encroachments of lands and illegal land reclamations carried out using political power.

* 	Immediate reacquisition by the Government of lands with commercial value, that have been allocated by the Mahaweli Authority of Sri Lanka 05 or more years ago, where no project has been yet implemented.

* 	Transfer of such the lands acquired to the Divisional Secretaries and provide them for the development activities of the people of the area under a structured programme.

* 	Preparation of a proper plan expeditiously to promote the tourism industry by utilizing the high potential of the eastern coastline, while ensuring the protection of eastern coastline.

* 	Formulation of a mechanism to ensure that the Public Officials enforce the law equitably and transparently in the operations of coastal hotels.

description: Final Budget Position Report (Annual Report) - 2025
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In accordance with the provisions of section 51 of the Public Financial Management Act, No.44 of 2024, a Final Budget Position Report for each financial year shall be released to the public and shall be published on the official website of the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development. Similarly, the said Report shall also be submitted to Parliament. Final Budget Position Report (Annual Report) - 2025 has been published by the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development. The said Report contains an analysis of the fiscal policy, strategies and challenges, economic developments in the year 2025, macroeconomic and socio-economic indicators covering all sectors of the economy and global economic developments. It also includes a detailed analysis of Government revenue and expenditure, cash flow management, financing of the budget deficit and debt structure. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to submit the Final Budget Position Report (Annual Report) - 2025 to Parliament, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the ‘Post-Cyclone Ditwah Reconstruction and Livelihoods Support Project’ with the financial assistance of the Asian Development Bank
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Cyclone Ditwah, which hit Sri Lanka in November 2025, caused severe damage to national infrastructure such as highways, railways and irrigation systems, as well as livelihoods, agricultural activities and housing. According to the Post-Disaster Needs Assessment conducted in this regard, the disaster caused approximately US$ 2.1 billion in damages and US$ 1.4 billion in economic losses, and the recovery needs are estimated at US$ 3.5 billion. Accordingly, taking into account the urgent recovery requirements and upon the request made by the Government of Sri Lanka, the Asian Development Bank has agreed to provide funding for the implementation of a project titled ‘Post-Cyclone Ditwah Reconstruction and Livelihoods Support Project’. The said project is planned to be implemented with three main components: Rehabilitation of cyclone -damaged road infrastructure, Reconstruction of cyclone-damaged irrigation systems, and Restoration of livelihoods and housing support. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to obtain funds of US$ 200 million for the proposed project, comprising US$ 100 million from Regular Ordinary Capital Resources and US$ 100 million from Concessional Ordinary Capital Resources, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Increasing the loan amount granted by the Asian Development Bank under the Policy Based Lending - 2026
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-03-16 to obtain US$ 380 million through the Asian Development Bank’s Policy-Based Lending during the year 2026. Out of this, US$ 100 million has been allocated for the Trade, Investment and Industrial Development Programme - Sub-Programme 1. However, amid the current economic uncertainty arising from the Middle East crisis and climate related shocks, the Asian Development Bank has agreed to provide assistance by increasing the loan amount under the said sub-programme to US$ 200 million through an additional financing package of US$ 100 million. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to take the relevant steps to obtain the said loan amount, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Revenue Protection Order made under the provisions of the Revenue Protection Act, No.19 of 1962, to Parliament for approval
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-02-23 to implement four customs import duty bands of 0%, 10%, 20%, and 30%, replacing the previously existed three-band structure, with the objective of promoting targeted growth in the country's export earnings, to implement the recommendations of the National Tariff Policy Committee and to implement New National Sub Divisions of HS Codes to support the development of the domestic agriculture and industrial sectors. The Revenue Protection                                   Order - No.01/2026 has been published through the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.2478/03 dated 2026-03-03, under the Revenue Protection Act, No.19 of 1962 laying down provisions for the aforesaid purpose. The proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to submit the said Revenue Protection Order to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of a new aqueduct type bridge across the Angamuwa Spillway (Ginipetti Palama) of the Thambuttegama - Rajanganaya Road
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The existing bridge (Ginipetti Palama) across Angamuwa Spillway on the Thambuttegama - Rajanganaya road is an aqueduct type bridge located on the Thambuttegama - Rajanganaya road, connecting the Anuradhapura - Padeniya road and the Anuradhapura -Puttalam road. The existing bridge trace is located on a relatively low-lying terrain, and the surrounding areas are affected by flooding during the rainy season, causing inconveniences to use the road. It has also been identified that the capacity of the said waterway is not sufficient to meet the future irrigation demand. Therefore, a project has been planned to construct a new aqueduct type bridge in place of the existing bridge across Angamuwa Spillway, with a higher capacity at the same location, using the provisions of the Eppawala, Giribawa, Rajanganaya and Nochchiyagama Integrated Water Supply Project implemented under the National Water Supply and Drainage Board. Accordingly, the joint proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development; and the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply to implement the proposed project at an estimated cost of Rs.241.45 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Programme to rebuild sacred places affected by the disaster ‘Ditwah’
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been reported that 758 Buddhist temples, 272 Hindu religious places, 199 Muslim religious places and 99 Christian religious places have suffered by various damages due to the 'Ditwah' disaster. Out of them, steps have been taken as of now to carry out renovation activities of 178 of these sacred places by utilizing funds of Rs.800 million allocated by the Buddhasasana Fund, the Central Cultural Fund and the Anagarika Dharmapala Foundation, including                Rs.200 million allocated as per the Cabinet decision dated 2026-04-27. The Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs to renovate another 90 sacred places out of the remaining places, using provisions of Rs.129.69 million, subject to the provisions of Circular No.01/2026 issued by the Ministry of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs.

description: Construction of a new building for the Divisional Secretariat, Negombo
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Divisional Secretariat, Negombo in the Gampaha District is currently operating in two 50-year-old buildings on a government-owned land within the Negombo Municipal Council area. 127 officers are employed in the office, and more than 1,500 people visit the office daily to obtain services. However, adequate space is not available in the Divisional Secretariat buildings for the officers to carry out their duties and to place office equipment and supplies. Also, due to the cracks, subsidence, water leakages etc. in the relevant buildings, the relevant staff has to work with great inconvenience and in a state of insecurity. Therefore, it has been identified as appropriate to establish the Divisional Secretariat, Negombo on a land of about one acre in the Udayarthoppuwa Grama Niladhari Division, where the Negombo Divisional Secretariat is currently located. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government to construct a new four-storey building for the Divisional Secretariat, Negombo on the said land at an estimated cost of Rs. 398.60 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Allocation of houses for the resettlement of families in the flood-prone Kolonnawa area and for the resettlement of unauthorized families residing on the underground oil pipeline of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The need has been identified to provide houses for 336 families in the Kolonnawa area who are frequently affected by floods and 72 families who are illegally residing on the underground oil pipeline belonging to the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation and are evicted from their current residences. The Road Development Authority has purchased 1,100 housing units from the Kolonnawa 'Sanhinda Sewana', Henamulla 'Helamuthu Sewana' and Maligawatta 'Lak hiru Sewana' housing projects implemented by the Urban Development Authority to provide them to the residents who will have to be evicted during the implementation of the project to construct the elevated expressway project connecting the Outer Circular Highway from the new Kelani Bridge to Athurugiriya. However, the project has been suspended due to an injunction granted by the Court of Appeal in relation to Phase II of the elevated expressway project. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to utilize 336 housing units of the Kolonnawa 'Sanhinda Sevana' Housing Project, which have been purchased for the said project, for the resettlement of families who are frequently affected by floods in the Kolonnawa area and 72 housing units of the Henamulla 'Helamuthu Sevana' Housing Project for the resettlement of families residing on the underground oil pipeline belonging to the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Resettlement of unauthorized dwellers affected by the land acquisition process for the construction of the Baseline Road Extension Project               Phase-III
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A committee chaired by the Divisional Secretary, Thimbirigasyaya has been appointed to provide houses to unauthorized families displaced due to the land acquisition process for the implementation of Phase III of the Baseline Road Extension Project.
