Based on the recommendations submitted by the said Committee, houses have been granted to 29 displaced family units as of now under the 'Sarasavi Uyana' housing scheme implemented by the Urban Development Authority. Considering the special circumstances and matters presented during the inspections such as the size of the house to be lost being more than the size of the house to be provided, several sub-families living in the same house at the time of land acquisition, and the presence of unmarried persons with special needs, the committee has recommended that houses be provided to 08 more displaced residents in addition to the 29 family units. The proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to implement the said recommendations, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Rehabilitation and improvement of a road section of the Badulla - Hali Ela Road
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Badulla-Chenkaladi Road Improvement Project is jointly financed by the OPEC Fund for International Development (OFID) and the Saudi Fund for Development (SFD). Approximately a loan saving of US$ 2.4 million is expected under the project for Ampara-Uhana-Mahaoya Road Improvement Project implemented through the funds of Saudi Fund for Development (SFD) under the above project. The proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development for the rehabilitation and improvement of a road section of 06 Km (from 115km to 121km) of the Badulla-Hali Ela road of the Peradeniya-Badulla-Chenkaladi road (A05), including a road section of 1.5 km (from 119+620 km to 121+200km) which has been utilized over a period of 15 years and has been severely damaged due to the Cylone Ditwah, under an estimated cost of Rs.600 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of facilities in School Hostels
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Out of the existing hostels in schools in the country, 126 hostel buildings are in old condition, and their maintenance and repairs are at a minimum level. It has been observed that the limited physical, sanitary, health and safety facilities available in school hostels have adversely affected the living conditions and educational performance of students residing in such hostels. Therefore, the need to modernize the essential facilities in the hostels and provide a quality environment for the education and health of the students has been identified. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education to implement a project to develop school hostel facilities during the period 2026-2028 at an estimated total cost of Rs. 1,008 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Preparation of a National Action Plan for the Management of HumanElephant Conflict
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Due to the loss of traditional migration routes of wild elephants and the destruction of their habitats owing to the reasons such as population growth, increase of development activities, and forest clearance in Sri Lanka during the past period, continuous and rapid increase in human-elephant conflicts has been observed in 19 out of 25 Districts and 134 out of 341 Divisional Secretariat Divisions of Sri Lanka for a long time. According to the Wild Elephant Survey conducted in 2024, it has been calculated that there are approximately 7,450 wild elephants in the country. It has been reported that a significant number of human lives and wild elephant deaths occur annually due to human-elephant conflicts. Similarly, more than a thousand cases of property damage caused by wild elephants are reported per year. Although a 'National Action Plan to Reduce Human-Elephant Conflict in Sri Lanka' was prepared in the year 2020, the need to prepare a new National Action Plan has been identified as the current human-elephant conflict situation has changed when compared to the said time period. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to take necessary steps to draft a new National Action Plan for the Management of Human-Elephant Conflict, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Hosting the 21st Steering Committee Meeting of the Cooperative Aviation Security Programme - Asia Pacific and the 14th Regional Aviation Security Coordination Forum - Asia and Pacific Regions, in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka has been invited to host two major regional aviation security events, the 21st Steering Committee Meeting of the Cooperative Aviation Security Programme - Asia Pacific (CASP-AP) and the 14th Regional Aviation Security Coordination Forum (RASCF) - Asia and Pacific Regions. The CASP-AP Steering Committee is the principal decision-making forum of the International Civil Aviation Organization’s Cooperative Aviation Security Programme in the Asia and Pacific Region. Sri Lanka is scheduled to assume the chairmanship of the Steering Committee for the period 2026-2027 at the said Conference. The Asia-Pacific Regional Aviation Security Coordination Forum serves as a regional platform for discussions on emerging threats, implementation of International Civil Aviation Organization Standards and recommended practices, capacity-building activities, and coordination among States and international organizations. Approximately 80 delegates, including representatives from 41 member countries, international organizations and observers, are scheduled to participate in the two events. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation to host the 21st Steering Committee Meeting of the Cooperative Aviation Security Programme - Asia and Pacific on 23rd and 24th June 2026 and the 14th Regional Aviation Security Coordination Forum - Asia and Pacific on 25th and 26th June 2026 in Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of the Bilateral Air Services Agreement signed between Sri Lanka and Türkiye
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Government of Sri Lanka and the Government of Türkiye signed an Air Services Agreement on 2008-12-02. In order to further develop the regulatory framework for air services between the two countries and to review aviation relations, both parties have subsequently held discussions wherein a consensus has been reached to amend Article 11 (Tariffs) of the existing Air Services Agreement. The Record of Discussion for this purpose was signed by the two parties on 2016-12-07. The clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the draft prepared for the proposed amendment to the said Agreement. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation to sign the amendment to the existing Air Services Agreement between Sri Lanka and Türkiye to prepare the tariff framework of the existing Air Services Agreement in line with internationally accepted standards, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment of a Senior Officials’ Committee to examine the feasibility of implementing all functions related to the Employees’ Provident Fund and the Employees’ Trust Fund under a Unified Governance Framework
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Employees’ Provident Fund, established under the Employees’ Provident Fund Act, No.15 of 1958, covers over 2.5 million members and has assets exceeding Rs. 4.9 trillion. The Central Bank of Sri Lanka is responsible for the custody, investment management, financial administration and payment of member benefits of the Employees’ Provident Fund, while the responsibility of registration of employers and employees, enforcement of compliance, recovery of dues and legal protection of employee rights under the Act is vested with the Department of Labour. The Employees’ Trust Fund, established under the Employees’ Trust Fund Act, No.46 of 1980, is governed by a Tripartite Board representing employers and employees. The said fund currently covers over 3 million active members and its assets exceed Rs.637.5 billion. Existence of a Tripartite Governance of social security is an internationally accepted best practice and is a key principle promoted by the International Labour Organization. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour to appoint a Senior Officials’ Committee to examine and make recommendations on the feasibility of bringing all the functions of the Employees’ Provident Fund and the Employees’ Trust Fund under a unified Governance framework under a Tripartite Board representing the Government, employers and employees, aligning with international best practices, while ensuring full legal and financial protection of the assets of the members, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Disposal of a block of land located at Keliyapura Grama Niladhari Division in the Hambantota Municipal Council limits for implementation of an Industrial and Container-related Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The block of land in extent of 108 acres 03 roods 37.85 perches, situated bordering the Hambantota-Gonnoruwa main road in the Keliyapura Grama Niladhari Division within the Hambantota Municipal Council limits in the Hambantota District, which has been transferred to the Urban Development Authority by way of a Grant under the provisions of section 6(1) of the State Lands Ordinance, has not been currently utilized for optimum use. The said block of land is located within the Central Commercial Zone of the Greater Hambantota Development Plan published by the Urban Development Authority. The Special Committee appointed to submit recommendations for the utilization of the currently unutilized lands owned by the Urban Development Authority for more suitable development activities, has recommended that an industrial, container and related development project be implemented on the said block of land. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to invite investment proposals following the international competitive bidding procedure to allocate the said block of land to suitable investors on a 50-year lease basis for the implementation of the proposed project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment to the Post of Director General of the Department of Management Audit
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A Committee has been appointed by the Secretary, Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to submit recommendations pertaining to the appointment of a suitable officer to the Post of Director General of the Department of Management Audit which has fallen vacant due to the retirement of Mr. A.P. Kurumbalapitiya who served in the said Post. The proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to appoint Mr. M.R.G.A.B. Muthukude, Special Grade Officer of the Sri Lanka Accountants’ Service, presently serving as the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Sri Lanka Customs, to the Post of Director General of the Department of Management Audit with immediate effect, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment to the Post of Director General of the Department of Information Technology Management
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A committee has been appointed by the Secretary, Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to make recommendations regarding the appointment of a suitable officer to the vacant post of Director General of the Department of Information Technology Management. Based on the recommendations made by the said Committee, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to appoint Mr. M.M.C.P. Mohottigedara, Special Grade Officer of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service, presently serving as the Additional Director General (Human Resource Management, Establishments, Cabinet and Parliament Affairs) of the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to the post of Director General of the Department of Information Technology Management, with immediate effect.

description: Appointment to a Post of Additional Secretary of the Prime Minister’s Office
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2024-12-02 for the appointment of Mrs. Chandani Sagarika Bogahawatta, Grade I Officer of the Sri Lanka Planning Service, to a Post of Additional Secretary of the Prime Minister’s Office, on full time acting basis. The Public Service Commission has promoted Mrs. Bogahawatta to the Special Grade of the Sri Lanka Planning Service with effect from 2026-01-01. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister to appoint Mrs. Chandani Sagarika Bogahawatte to a Post of Additional Secretary in the Prime Minister's Office on permanent basis, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Drafting a Bill for Biosafety to minimize and avoid effects of genetically modified organisms resulting from modern biotechnology to biodiversity and human health
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety was established in 2000 by the stakeholder States to the Convention on Biological Diversity, with the aim of minimizing the potential adverse impacts of genetically modified organisms generated by modern biotechnology on human health, biodiversity conservation and sustainable use and ensuring adequate protection against such hazards. Since Sri Lanka is also a stakeholder state to the said Convention, a local legal framework needs to be prepared to minimize the potential impacts on biodiversity conservation caused by Genetically Modified Organisms. Accordingly, approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2021-08-09 to make further amendments required to the Biodiversity Bill, which had been prepared by the Legal Draftsman as per the Cabinet decision dated 2017-09-12. Taking into account the proposal made by the Minister of Environment, it was decided to grant policy approval of the Cabinet to expeditiously complete the preparation of the final Bill, by incorporating further appropriate provisions into the Bill already drafted by the Legal Draftsman as per the said Cabinet decision.

description: Submission of the Anti-Corruption (Declarations of Assets and Liabilities through the Centralized Electronic System) Regulations made under section 156 of the Anti-Corruption Act, No.9 of 2023
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-03-30 to proclaim through a Gazette Notification, the Anti-Corruption (Declarations of Assets and Liabilities through the Centralized Electronic System) Regulations and the Anti-Corruption (High-risk Categories Required to Submit the Declaration of Assets and Liabilities) Regulations made under the provisions of the Anti-Corruption Act, No.9 of 2023. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice and National Integration to submit the said Regulations published through the Gazette Extraordinary Notifications Nos. 2482/03 and 2482/04 dated 2026-03-30, to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Customs Ordinance
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-05-26 to establish the Revenue Administration Reforms and Modernization Bureau and to appoint separate Steering Committees for the Department of Customs, Department of Inland Revenue and Excise Department thereunder, with the objective of creating and establishing a global level revenue administration mechanisms in the country, Accordingly, the Steering Committee on Customs Affairs has submitted recommendations on the restructuring and modernization activities to be implemented in Sri Lanka Customs. The said Committee has recommended that an Expert Committee should be appointed to conduct an indepth study on the Customs Ordinance, identify outdated provisions, determine the provisions that require timely amendment, and recommend necessary amendments to the Customs Ordinance, taking into account the views and suggestions of the business community, the import and export sector and other stakeholders. Accordingly, representing all relevant sectors, the Customs Ordinance Review Committee has been appointed under the Chairmanship of the President's Counsel, Retired Additional Solicitor General Milinda Gunathilaka. The Committee has met continuously for nearly 07 months, discussed with all relevant parties and submitted a detailed Report. Based on the recommendations of the said Report, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a Bill to amend the Customs Ordinance, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Proclamation of Regulations/Order under the provisions of the Foreign Exchange Act, No.12 of 2017
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- On the recommendations of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka, the Foreign Exchange (Classes of Capital Transactions Undertaken Outside Sri Lanka by a person resident in Sri Lanka) Regulations No.1 of 2021 and Foreign Exchange (Remittance of Funds by Emigrants) Regulations No.3 of 2021 have been issued under the provisions of the Foreign Exchange Act, No.12 of 2017, by granting a general permission for capital transactions undertaken outside Sri Lanka by residents in Sri Lanka and permission for the outward remittances by emigrants. Outward remittances made upon the permission granted under the said Regulations have been subjected to various restrictions as per an Order under the provisions of section 22 of the Foreign Exchange Act, which has been published by the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.2467/67 and dated 2025-12-18. The Central Bank of Sri Lanka has recommended that the existing Regulations under the Foreign Exchange Act be repealed and new Regulations be issued, and that a new Order be issued to continue the restrictions currently in force. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to publish the following Regulations/Order under the provisions of the Foreign Exchange Act through Government Gazette Notifications, was approved by the Cabinet:

Foreign Exchange (Overseas Investments Made by Persons Resident in Sri Lanka) Regulations, No.1 of 2026.


Foreign Exchange (Fund Transfers Abroad by Emigrants) Regulations, No.2 of 2026.


Order under the provisions of section 22 of the Foreign Exchange Act, No.12 of 2017.

description: Preparation of a Digital Economy Bill to accelerate Digital Transformation and Digital Economy Development
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - An institutional framework with legal powers is essential to ensure the effective implementation of the National Digital Policy and Guidelines. The institutional framework should attract quality human capital in the spheres of policy making, technology implementation, operational regulation and enforcement. In the preparation of a strong institutional framework, the continued participation of the private sector should also be considered, and it has also been recognized that it should focus on new areas of digital innovation, including support for the development of artificial intelligence and related activities. Taking those factors into account, a Concept Paper has been prepared to draft the Digital Economy Bill to establish a new institutional framework. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Digital Economy to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare the draft Digital Economy Bill, based on the said concept paper, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Project on Construction and Maintenance of Public Toilet Systems under the Local Authorities Island Wide under the Clean Sri Lanka Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-01-06 to implement the Project on Improvement of Sanitation Facilities for the General Public and Tourists in Urban Areas. Accordingly, the Ministry of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government has implemented 29 project proposals in the year 2025 from the provisions of Rs.327 million provided under the Clean Sri Lanka Programme. Out of the 29 projects, construction works of 16 projects have been completed as of now, and the construction works of the remaining projects are scheduled to be completed during ensuing month. After evaluating the feasibility of the project proposals submitted by the Local Government Authorities island wide for this year as well, with regard to improving sanitation facilities for the general public and tourists in urban areas, it has been agreed to allocate provisions amounting to Rs.150 million under the Clean Sri Lanka Programme for the implementation of 26 projects in 24 local government areas on priority basis during the year 2026. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government for the implementation of the said projects, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of the Pitipana - Thalagala Road
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The ‘Tech City Project’ in Homagama, Pitipana, Mahenawatta has been initiated with the objective of making a high contribution to the country’s economy based on innovation and knowledge-centred technology. Under its first phase, a block of land in extent of  236 acres has been acquired by the Urban Development Authority, and it has been allocated for the establishment of institutions such as the Green University, the Faculties of Technology of the Universities of Colombo and Sri Jayewardenepura, the Sri Lanka Institute of Nanotechnology, the Sri Lanka Institute of Biotechnology, the Department of Measurement Units, Standards and Services and Mahinda Rajapaksa College, with the aim of transforming the said land into an  innovation hub that promotes technical education, industry, innovation and competitiveness. At present, nearly 50,000 people visit this area daily, and it is predicted that significantly higher number of people will visit the area daily by the time the project is completed as planned. Therefore, the need to expand the existing road network has been identified, and among them, the Pitipana-Talagala road has to be given priority. Accordingly, the joint proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development and the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government to take urgent steps to widen the narrow road of about 30 feet width from the School Junction to the Textbook Warehouse on the same road with 02 lanes, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Sri Lanka Demographic and Health Survey - 2026/2027
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Demographic and Health Survey is the main data source for reviewing the progress towards achieving the national health development goals as well as the global Sustainable Development Goals to be achieved by 2030. The said Survey was last conducted in 2016, and the Sri Lanka Demographic and Health Survey has to be conducted to obtain updated data so that data and indicators related to the health and well-being targets of the global Sustainable Development Goals can be provided promptly. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to take necessary steps to conduct the said survey, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: National Water Tariff Policy applicable to all Water Supply and Sanitation Services
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Access to safe, reliable and affordable drinking water and adequate sanitation facilities is essential to maintain public health, promote social welfare and foster economic development. The Government of Sri Lanka recognizes water supply and sanitation services as both an economic good and a basic human need. Therefore, in setting tariff for water and sanitation services, a proper balance between the financial sustainability of service providers and the need to ensure equitable and affordable access for all segments of the society should be maintained. Accordingly, the Government of Sri Lanka has identified the need for a National Water Tariff Policy applicable to all water supply and sanitation service providers and sensitive to gender equality and social inclusion. Currently, there is no formal national framework for setting tariff for water supply systems operated by various water service providers as well as for price setting, review, approval and implementation for sanitation systems. Therefore, the Ministry of Housing, Construction and Water Supply has prepared a National Water Tariff Policy covering all water supply service providers under the Sri Lanka Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Reform Programme, a policy-based loan programme implemented under the funds of the Asian Development Bank. The proposal made by the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply to implement the said National Water Tariff Policy, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: National Policy on Green Hydrogen in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Green hydrogen, produced via water electrolysis powered by renewable energy, is now globally recognized as the ‘fuel of the future’ for decarbonizing shipping, aviation and heavy industries. It has been estimated that Sri Lanka possesses a massive offshore wind potential exceeding 56 GW, which far surpasses domestic electricity needs. This surplus renewable energy can be harnessed to produce green hydrogen, and Sri Lanka has the potential to launch green hydrogen production projects and access global export routes by leveraging its geographical location. Accordingly, a draft policy framework for the green hydrogen sector has been prepared, taking into account the views and responses of the public, other relevant parties and the Department of National Planning, as per the approval granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-08-11. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Energy for the implementation of the said National Policy and for the preparation of the Road Map, Work Flow and Regulations in that regard, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the ‘Women Empowerment Targeted Programme’ as per the Budget Proposals 2026
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Women's Bureau of Sri Lanka that comes under the purview of the Ministry of Women and Child Affairs implements the 'Empowering Women through Entrepreneurship Development' programme, targeting women in economically vulnerable groups. In parallel, provisions of Rs.200 million have been allocated for the 'Women Empowerment Targeted Programme' under the budget proposals 2026. Under the said programme, it has been planned to carry out mainly in encouraging intermediate-level women entrepreneurs to become high-level entrepreneurs, creating local and foreign market opportunities, economically empowering women of middle-income earner category under public private partnership, directing unemployed young women towards entrepreneurship, providing relief to women affected by gender-based violence and the capacity development of officers. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Acting Minister of Women and Child Affairs to implement the proposed programme in accordance with the Annual Implementation Plan - 2026, which has been prepared under 11 main programme areas, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Memorandum of Cooperation between Sri Lanka and Japan on the Employment for Skills Development Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In order to secure skilled and semi-skilled human resources required for key sectors of the Japanese economy due to demographic decline, increasing aging population and shrinking domestic workforce, the Government of Japan has introduced several foreign labour mobility schemes. Accordingly, under the Cooperation Agreements signed between Sri Lanka and Japan in 2017 and 2019 with the approval of the Cabinet, Sri Lankan workers are employed in Japan under the Technical Inter Training Programme and the Specific Skilled Worker Programme. The Government of Japan has decided to introduce a new programme called the 'Employment for Skills Development Programme’ with a more transparent, worker-oriented and sustainable labour mobility framework, to be effective from 2027-04-01. Under the said programme, provisions have been made available for enhanced worker protection, cleaner career pathways and opportunities for transition to the Specific Skilled Worker Programme. The proposal made by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism to enter into a Cooperation Agreement between the two countries to provide opportunities for Sri Lankans as well, to work in Japan under the said programme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Project for Integrated Systematic Approach
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Although attention has been paid to the protection and education of children aged 2 years or above in the families of women who migrate for employment, it has been observed that attention paid to the sustainable development of such families is inadequate. Further, even if such women return to the country at the end of their employment contract period, there is a tendency for them to go abroad again and again to fulfil their economic and social goals due to the lack of a proper plan for family development. It has also been observed that the measures to be taken regarding the protection of children between the ages of 3 and 18 should be implemented in a more systematic manner through a proper mechanism. Therefore, the need to implement a development programme for the long-term prosperity of migrant worker families has been identified. Accordingly, a project called ‘Integrated Systematic Approach for the Development of Migrant Worker Families’ has been planned to be implemented by relevant Government officials by working together as a single team to provide guidance and facilities to migrant worker families relating to the matters such as economic guidance, child health and protection, women’s affairs, vocational training, small enterprise development and export development. The proposal made by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism to prepare and implement a Five Year Development Plan to provide a sustainable living standard for the foreign workers' families that are in a situation that requires special attention through the said project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of Upper Watershed Area Management Authority
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Cyclone Ditwah, which caused devastating impacts on Sri Lanka, caused extensive damages to human lives, properties, infrastructure and agriculture, and it has been reported that 34% of the sensitive natural forest areas in the central highlands have been destroyed due to landslides and strong winds caused by the storm. The destruction has severely affected the ecosystems of 07 major river basins. As a result, it has been identified that there is a serious risk of soil erosion and drying up of natural water sources in those areas. Taking into consideration the need to take urgent measures to alleviate the said situation, which has been aggravated by decades of improper land use, it has been proposed to establish a separate Authority for the management of upper watershed areas. The objective of the said Authority is to develop and implement a long-term protection programme for such areas in a manner that aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals while enhancing resilience to adverse climate conditions. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President to appoint a Technical Expert Committee to formally identify the institutional structure and functional scope of the Upper Watershed Area Management Authority, to prepare a draft Bill for the said purpose, and to establish the Upper Watershed Management Area Authority under a Three-Phased Implementation Plan, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between the Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism and Hotel Management and the Central Academy of Culture and Tourism Administration of the People’s Republic of China
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism and Hotel Management, functioning under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism, has initiated a collaboration with the Central Academy of Culture and Tourism Administration of the People's Republic of China with the aim of establishing a policy framework for institutional cooperation in areas including academic exchange, professional training, collaborative research, faculty development and sharing of knowledge resources. A Memorandum of Understanding has been drafted, including the observations of the Attorney General as well to regularize the said cooperation. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism to sign the proposed Memorandum of Understanding between the Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism and Hotel Management and the Central Academy of Culture and Tourism Administration of the People's Republic of China, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Programme for empowering people affected by the disaster
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2025 12 05, granted approval for the implementation of the programme for empowering those affected by the disaster to restore the livelihood that was disrupted due to the sudden disaster situation caused by the Cyclone Ditwah. The proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to pursue action as follows to address the issues identified while reviewing the progress of the empowerment programme held in several Districts that were most affected by the said sudden disaster situation, was approved by the Cabinet:

* 	to issue necessary Circular instructions enabling to extend the monthly house rent allowance provided for a maximum period of 06 months to homeowners who lost their houses and do not own a house for residence, up to a maximum period of 09 months to temporarily settle in another place until they are able to construct their own houses.

* 	to issue Circulars and instructions regarding the removal of rocks, soil and debris accumulated on paddy lands and restore the said paddy lands to suitable condition for cultivation after obtaining the approval of relevant institutions as per an estimate approved for the same by the District Deputy Commissioner/Assistant Commissioner of Agrarian Development.

* 	to use the provisions allocated under the Landslide Mitigation Programme under the Ministry of Defence with priority to carry out landslide risk mitigation activities in locations where rock falls and earth slips have occurred or in areas prone to landslides, as recommended by the National Building Research Organization.

* 	to provide the necessary provisions appropriately through the provisions allocated for disaster relief and rehabilitation activities by the General Treasury.

description: Declaration of Elephant Corridors in Monaragala and Hambantota Districts to minimize human-elephant conflicts
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Wild elephants live in about 2/3 of the country's land area, and the rapid blockage of wild elephant habitats and migration routes due to various development projects and human activities has directly affected the escalation of elephant-human conflicts. It has been identified that the protection of wild elephant habitats and migration routes should be done urgently to minimize such conflicts to some extent. The Department of Wildlife Conservation, in collaboration with the relevant Divisional Secretaries, stakeholder institutions and organizations, is currently identifying the migration routes of wild elephants. Under the programme to identify wild elephant migration routes in the Monaragala District, the wild elephant migration route from Handapanagala to the Yala National Park via the Menik River in Demodara has been identified, and the approval for the same has also been received from the Monaragala District Coordination Committee. The elephant migration route from Lunugamvehera National Park in Zone VI of the Yala National Park to Udawalawe National Park was declared as the Wetahira Kanda Wildlife Sanctuary in the year 2002. 05 plots of land with land permits have been identified in the relevant area, and these lands have not been developed yet. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to take the following steps, was approved by the Cabinet:

* 	To declare the elephant migration route from Handapanagala in the Monaragala District to the Yala National Park via the Menik River in Demodara as a sanctuary under the provisions of the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance.

*	To re-declare the Watahira Kanda Nature Reserve as a 'Forest Gateway' by providing alternative lands at a suitable location outside the wildlife reserve, instead of 05 plots of land with land permits located within the Watahira Kanda Nature Reserve Area.

*	To acquire the plots of land including the buildings constructed blocking the Koholankala Elephant corridor in the Hambantota District by paying compensation and declare the area belonging to the Hambantota Wild Elephant Management Reserve as a sanctuary.

description: Submission of the Imports and Exports (Control) Regulations No.04 of 2026 to Parliament for approval
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Hydrochlorofluorocarbons, chemical compound widely used in refrigerators and air conditioning units, are being phased out globally under the Montreal Protocol due to their ozone-depletion and high global warming potential. Accordingly, Sri Lanka is also committed to phase out this series of chemicals by 2030. Accordingly, the Imports and Exports (Control) Regulations No.04 of 2026 under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, No.1 of 1969 has been published through the Gazette Extraordinary Notification dated 2026 05 07, to ban the importation of equipment and accessories operating exclusively with hydrochlorofluorocarbons with effect from 06-06-2026 and to prohibit the import of compressors operating exclusively with hydrochlorofluorocarbons used as a component of the refrigeration system for equipment and accessories with effect from 01-01-2028. The proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to submit the said Regulations to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Small Towns and Rural Water Supply Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Access to safe drinking water has yet to be fully realized for the people residing in small towns and rural areas of Sri Lanka, which remains a major challenge affecting the social and economic development of the country. It has been planned to implement a programme to provide clean drinking water to about 600,000 families living in semi-urban and rural areas through 300 projects covering 50 small towns and rural areas, redressing the said situation.  The projects aim to establish safe, reliable and sustainable drinking water supply systems, and it is expected to treat the water using modern treatment technologies including chlorination and filtration systems in accordance with national and international drinking water standards. Accordingly, taking into consideration a proposal submitted by the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply, the Cabinet granted its approval for the proposed programme to be implemented by the National Water Supply and Drainage Board and the Department of National Community Water Supply during the period 2027-2029 by conducting a feasibility study on the said programme and including it in the Public Investment Programme based on its results.

description: Awarding the procurement for the supply of Lubricating Oil for Sapugaskanda Power Station for a period of 2026/27
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026 02 09 to implement the procurement for the supply of lubricating oil to Plant A and Plant B of the Sapugaskanda Power Station for the period of 2026/27. Accordingly, bids have been invited following the National Competitive Procurement Methodology, and 03 bids have been received for the same. The proposal made by the Minister of Energy to award the relevant procurements as follows, based on the recommendations made by the High Level Procurement Committee, after evaluating the said bids, was approved by the Cabinet:
*	Awarding the contract for the supply of 316,000 liters of lubricating oil to Plant A of the Sapugaskanda Power Station to Lanka IOC PLC, the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, for a sum of Rs.392.47 million (inclusive of VAT).

* 	Awarding the contract for the supply of 304,000 liters of lubricating oil to Plant B of the Sapugaskanda Power Station to Chevron Lubricants Lanka PLC, the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, for a sum of Rs.434.86 million (inclusive of VAT).

description: Awarding the Contract for the Construction of Lot A of the Mullikulam Wind Power Transmission Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025 02 03 to implement the Mullikulam Wind Power Transmission Project. The project consists of two projects, namely Lot A and Lot B and the contract for the construction of Lot B of the project has been awarded by now. Bids have been invited following the International Competitive Procurement Methodology for the construction of Lot A, which includes the incomer side of the Mullikulam 220/33 kV Collector Grid Substation and the Construction of 02 Nos. of 220 kV Line Bays at the said Grid Substation. 04 bids have been received for the same. The proposal made by the Minister of Energy to award the said contract to RS Infraprojects (Pvt) Ltd. of India, the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, for a sum of US$ 6.04 million and Sri Lankan Rupees 499.66 million (excluding VAT) based on the recommendation submitted by the High Level Procurement Committee after evaluating the said bids, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Project for the construction of the Amaradeva Aesthetic and Research Centre (Amaradeva Asapuwa)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The construction of the Amaradeva Aesthetics and Research Centre (Amaradeva Asapuwa) was initiated by the then Ministry of Mass Media as a special budget proposal presented in the year 2017, in grateful recognition of the invaluable national contribution rendered by Dr. Pandit Amaradeva to the field of music in Sri Lanka. Although about 09 years have elapsed since the construction work began, it has not been completed yet. Although the General Treasury has provided a provision of Rs.226.18 million in the year 2025 to complete the relevant construction work and purchase essential office equipment, only Rs.141.54 million of the said provisions has been spent in the year 2025. The proposal made by the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs to secure provisions of Rs.113.17 million to complete all work of the project within this year, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of 25 Towns under the 'Mithuru Purawara Programme'
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - According to the 2026 Budget Proposals, more attention has been placed on urban development, and a development programme titled 'Mithuru Purawara' has been proposed to be implemented thereunder. The said programme, which is centered on the objective of 'development of small towns for the convenience and well-being of the public and local communities', is expected to identify one essential development activity in each of 25 selected towns in the island and complete it during the year 2026. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to allocate an estimated amount of Rs. 581 million under the 'Clean Sri Lanka' programme for the implementation of the projects identified in 23 towns identified for implementation in the initial phase of the 'Mithuru Purawara' programme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Rehabilitation and Improvement of the Road Lighting System of the Colombo - Katunayake Expressway, Including the Kerawalapitiya Interchange
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The road lighting system on the Colombo-Katunayake Expressway, including the Kerawalapitiya Interchange, has suffered significant damage due to persistent vandalism and theft, mainly carried out by drug addicts, and approximately 85% of the lighting system is currently non-functional. Therefore, considering the cost of lighting the entire length of the expressway, it has been planned to light only the Peliyagoda, Kerawalapitiya, Seeduwa and Ja-Ela interchanges as well as the freeway sections from the New Kelani Bridge to the Peliyagoda Fish Market and from Seeduwa to the Bandaranaike International Airport in the first phase. The proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to have the rehabilitation and improvement of the lighting system of those road sections carried out in two packages at an estimated cost of Rs.1,098.50 million, through contractors selected following the National Competitive Procurement Methodology, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Projects identified under the Development of 10 Cities Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- The Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development has been allocated Rs.1,300 million through the 2026 budget to redevelop the attractive cities identified in Sri Lanka as model cities, highlighting their heritage and identity, and to popularize them among local and foreign tourists through city branding. Accordingly, the said project is expected to be implemented based on a study conducted by a suitable consultancy firm based on the concept of City Branding, highlighting the identity and uniqueness of the cities of Anuradhapura, Kataragama, Colombo and Kandy. For the purpose, it is estimated that about Rs.325 million will be spent for the year 2026.

Also, the 2026 budget has proposed to implement the 10 Cities Development Programme as well with the aim of promoting a systematic, prioritized and data driven approach in the field of urban development. Under the said programme, 217 prioritized projects identified in the cities of Jaffna, Matale, Hatton, Batticaloa, Chilaw, Thambuttegama, Vavuniya, Eheliyagoda, Badulla and Matara have been planned to be implemented. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to expeditiously implement the projects identified under the 10 Cities Development Programme for the year 2026, using a total of Rs.1,475 million, comprising the remaining Rs.975 million of the provisions allocated for the budget 2026 for the City Branding Project and including the Rs.500 million allocated for the development of Hatton and Matale cities, since development of those cities are also covered under this programme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Digitalization of the plans of 3.5 million land plots available in hard copy form at the Survey Department of Sri Lanka and their integration into the Land Information System
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It is estimated that there are about 16 million plots of land in Sri Lanka. Of these, about 6 million plots of land have been surveyed so far, and the information on about 2.5 million of them is available in digitized format. The data has been entered into a Land Information System and published on the website of the Survey Department of Sri Lanka. With the aim of improving land management efficiency and decision-making capacity by providing access to accurate and verifiable land information to government institutions, stakeholders and the public, a project has been planned to digitize the information on the remaining 3.5 million plots of land in hard copy form, which have been surveyed since 1800, and enter them into the Land Information System. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation for the implementation of the proposed project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Updated Guidelines for the Sri Lanka National Green Reporting System
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - With the aim of promoting sustainable performance in the manufacturing and service sectors, the 'National Green Reporting System' was established in the year 2012 with the approval of the Cabinet. For the purpose, the third generation standards of 2011 of the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), which is an international sustainable reporting framework, were adopted as the basis. Since the standards of the International Sustainable Reporting Framework have been updated by 2025 and taking into account the current global trends such as climate change, Sustainable Development Goals and obligations related to the Paris Agreement, the need to revise the National Green Reporting System has been identified. Accordingly, measures have been taken to update the International Sustainable Reporting Guidelines, consisting of a total of 76 indicators, including 31 environmental indicators, 30 social indicators and 15 governance indicators. Similarly, 05 reporting levels have been introduced for institutions that agree to follow the National Green Reporting System. Measures have also been taken to re-constitute the National Green Reporting Steering Committee with 24 members, including the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka and the Sustainable Development Council of Sri Lanka. Accordingly, Cabinet decided to grant its concurrence to implement the updated Sri Lanka National Green Reporting System and the Guidelines referred to above, submitted by the Minister of Environment for the attention of the Cabinet.

description: Revised National Oil and Hazardous and Noxious Substance Spill Contingency Plan and its Digital Platform
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been observed that with over 400 vessels transiting daily in the East-West maritime routes located adjacent to Sri Lanka and over 5000 ships calling at Sri Lankan ports annually, expansion of existing ports, growth in oil-related activities and the impact of global climate change, there is a risk of oil and hazardous and noxious substances spilling in the Sri Lankan waters in the future, thereby causing a marine environmental damage. As per the provisions of the Marine Pollution Prevention Act, No.35 of 2008, it is a duty of the Marine Environment Protection Authority to formulate and implement a scheme to prevent such pollution in the Sri Lankan waters. Accordingly, the National Oil Spill Contingency Plan, previously prepared as per the said provisions upon the approval of the Cabinet, has been revised, having included response mechanisms for Hazardous and Noxious Substances. Similarly, the first phase of the Digital Platform of the said National Plan has also been prepared. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to implement the proposed National Plan on an instance of an Oil and Hazardous & Noxious Substance Spill Contingency, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Waste Management within the Coastal Zone including the Fishery Harbours in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- The improper disposal of waste, including large quantities of waste, plastic discharged from the inland areas of the country into the ocean through rivers and waterways, together with the improper disposal of large quantities of fibreglass waste near fishery harbours, ferries and anchorage points, which has led to numerous health, social and environmental problems, has placed the sensitive ecosystems spread across the coastal zone of Sri Lanka under threat. Although there are several number of institutions for solid waste management in the coastal zone of the island, as a solution to the problem of lack of proper coordination between these institutions, the Marine Environment Protection Authority has established the National Committee for Waste Management in Coastal areas including fishery harbours and 84 regional committees by involving Local Government institutions in coastal districts. Accordingly, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to take the following steps regarding waste management within the coastal zone:

*	To implement the 'Proposal for Waste Management in Coastal Zone and Fishery Harbours' prepared by the Marine Environment Protection Authority in collaboration with the institutions belonging to the National Committee and other stakeholder institutions.

* 	To use the mobile app developed to more efficiently fulfil the responsibilities included in the proposal.

* 	To take necessary action to amend the Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Act, No.2 of 1996 and the Marine Pollution Prevention Act, No.35 of 2008 to introduce and implement the principle of 'Extended Producer Responsibility' to assign responsibilities for the proper disposal of fiberglass waste.

description: Construction of the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit on the Fourth Floor at the new Paediatric Ward Complex at the Teaching Hospital - Ratnapura
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Ratnapura Teaching Hospital, the main tertiary healthcare provider in the Sabaragamuwa Province, provides a wide range of medical services and, as it is currently affiliated to the University of Sabaragamuwa, also contributes to advancing medical education and research. As per the approval given at the Cabinet meeting held on 2016-07-26, a Memorandum of Understanding has been signed with local donors who have offered to provide financial assistance for the construction of a five-storied building for the Paediatric Ward Complex of the said hospital and accordingly, construction work has been carried out up to the third floor of the said building. Local donors have again come forward to provide financial assistance for the construction of the fourth floor of the new ward complex to establish the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit. The recommendation of the Department of National Planning has also been received for the relevant project. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Health and Mass Media and the relevant donors to implement the project to construct the 'Paediatric Intensive Care Unit' on the fourth floor of the new Paediatric Ward Complex at the Teaching Hospital, Ratnapura, by obtaining funding contributions of Rs.64.15 million, which is the total estimated cost of the project, from local donors, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Enhancing community access through Arogya Wellness Centres
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka's health needs are rapidly changing due to the ongoing demographic and epidemiological transitions, resulting in a triple burden of non communicable diseases, communicable diseases and injuries. Sri Lanka’s primary care delivery, which is divided between the public and private sectors, predominantly operates on a model that focuses mainly on treating acute conditions. Although, the Universal Health Coverage Service Index of Sri Lanka, remains lower than expected, it is above the regional average. Accordingly, with the objective of increasing disease control and free healthcare access, the Ministry of Health and Mass Media has planned to establish 'Arogya Health and Wellness Centres' in line with the vision of 'A Thriving Nation-A Beautiful Life'. As decided at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-09-15 and also taking into account the recommendations made by the Committee appointed to submit recommendations for the more effective and efficient implementation of the proposed project to increase community access through Arogya Health and Wellness Centers, the joint proposal made by the Minister of Labour and the Acting Minister if Health and Mass Media to establish 1,000 Arogya Health and Wellness Centers during the period 2026-2028 in a phased out manner thereby increasing the total number of primary care institutions, including the existing regional hospitals and primary medical care units, to 2,000 and to provide the necessary human and physical resources for the said centers, was approved by the Cabinet.
